div.head: Paper Prepared in the National Security Council

p.hi: OPTIONS FOR HANDLING KRASNOYARSK AND THE ISSUE OF MATERIAL BREACH

div.p: I. AT THE REVIEW, the U.S. delegation should take the following steps.

list.label: a.
list.item: Reiterate that the Krasnoyarsk radar is a significant violation of a central element of the ABM Treaty, essential to the treaty’s object and purpose.
list.label: b.
list.item: Clearly make the point that the Krasnoyarsk violation will continue to raise questions of material breach and proportional response until resolved [and that if the Soviets cannot provide any satisfaction with respect to the Krasnoyarsk issue at this review, following the review, the United States will have to consider declaring this continuing violation as a material breach of the treaty (Option 1)].
list.label: c.
list.item: State that, in this connection, the United States reserves all rights, consistent with international law, to take appropriate and proportionate responses at a later time should the Soviets continue to refuse to correct the violation.
list.label: d.
list.item: Further state, for the record, that there will be no START or Defense & Space Treaties until this violation is resolved.
list.label: e.
list.item: Be prepared to tell the Soviets what specific steps the United States expects the Soviet Union to take to dismantle in a verifiable fashion the Krasnoyarsk radar.
list.label: f.
list.item: Ask the Soviets what they are prepared to do to resolve this situation promptly.

div.p: II. AFTER THE REVIEW (assuming no satisfactory response from the Soviet Union), the President would issue publicly a arms control policy statement making the following main points.

list.label: a.
list.item: Based on the just concluded ABM Treaty review, the United States considers the Krasnoyarsk radar to be a significant violation of a central element of the ABM Treaty, essential to the treaty’s object and purpose.
list.label: b.
list.item: [Since the Soviet Union has given no indication of any willingness to correct this violation, the United States has no alternative but to identify it for what it is, a material breach of the ABM Treaty. (Option 1)]

div.p: [The Krasnoyarsk violation will continue to raise questions of material breach and proportional response until resolved. (Option 2)]

list.label: c.
list.item: While it would be fully justified in doing so, the United States does not intend to take an appropriate response at this time to this [material breach (Option 1)] [significant violation (Option 2)], rather it will once again go the extra mile to give the Soviet Union additional time (amount unspecified) to reverse its position and act responsibly.
list.label: d.
list.item: The United States reserves all rights, consistent with international law, to take appropriate and proportionate responses at a later time should the Soviets continue to refuse to correct the violation.
list.label: e.
list.item: In any case, it is the position of the United States that there will be no START or Defense & Space Treaties until this violation is resolved.

div.p: III. AFTER THE REVIEW (assuming no satisfactory response from the Soviet Union), in parallel with the PUBLIC arms control policy statement the President would issue an INTERNAL study directive including the following elements.

list.label: a.
list.item: The Department of Defense, working with other agencies as appropriate, should develop an options paper which presents a range of proportionate responses (programmatic and otherwise) from which the President could choose should the Soviets resume construction of the Krasnoyarsk radar or otherwise refuse to correct this violation.
list.label: b.
list.item: During the first three weeks of this activity, a plan should be developed and promptly submitted for Presidential approval on how best to involve the Congress in the options development and review process.
list.label: c.
list.item: As the study continues and options are developed, for programmatic responses, the options should be described in sufficient detail so that, should the President decide to execute one of the options, implementation steps could begin without further study.
list.label: d.
list.item:
Individual options should be developed as quickly as possible. They should be presented to the President for his consideration, as a
hedge against all contingencies, as soon as each has been thoroughly staffed, evaluated and coordinated.
list.label: e.
list.item: The overall study, and a comprehensive evaluation of all options developed, should be completed by the end of this calendar year.
